scope: Independently measure all four actual paired-skill trajectories in each of the 40 registered, later training-history windows (378 distinct questions). Use 251 physical GPU 4 for the Qwen encoder at batch at most two/duty 0.30 and the serial BF16 Llama service on GPUs 5 and 6 at duty 0.28, with separate cache keys and measurements from the GPU 7 study. Keep 2 GiB encoder headroom and the two-GPU server's 4608 MiB reserve. Keep every question and the ordered K=3 writer action. No training, tuning or independent test data enter this replication.
timing: Start with windows whose original randomized pair has already finished. Before measuring any other window, require the full single-rank witness policy's numeric forecast for all target sessions. Exclude a window from a stage's strictly prospective panel if ANY branch of either backend had a registered score before that stage's forecast. Later research must count this additional archive when declaring pre-exposure. Reference and replica scores stay separate.
estimands: For each of four physical writer/reader paths verify every selected skill, versioned memory, reader response, prompt, token count, answer and score. Check that the root decision context is identical across all four and the second state is the same for paths with the same first action. Evaluate the learned group/witness, raw, rotated, unpaired, group-only, native and terminal models in actual reached states. Compute the two-step exact expected F1 as the sum over all four path masses, with design-weighted and local randomized contrasts separately. Also take one shared, predeclared uniform draw per window and chronological position to report path changes and sampled-policy F1. Compare the original randomized arms' answers across the two backends when available; logged disagreement remains visible. Report all 40 windows, per-type and per-history results and paired whole-history intervals. This additional six-history trial cannot replace the independent complete tests.
